findings.title: Authorization check uses AND instead of OR, blocking legitimate team admins/owners
findings.body: The variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` (logical AND) between `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)`. This means a user must be BOTH a team admin AND a team owner to pass this check. A team admin who is not an owner (or vice versa) will be denied access. The intent, as indicated by the variable name and the error message on line 55, is clearly to allow either role. The operator should be `||` (logical OR).

findings.title: Passes unfiltered `guests` to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of `uniqueGuests`
findings.body: On line 168, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw `guests` input array. However, `guests` may contain emails that were filtered out on lines 74-78 (already-existing attendees or blacklisted emails). The email function uses this list to decide whether each attendee receives a 'new booking' email (`AttendeeScheduledEmail`) or a 'guests added' notification (`AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`). Passing the unfiltered list means already-existing attendees whose email appears in `guests` will incorrectly receive a full booking confirmation email instead of the 'new guests added' notification. The correct argument is `uniqueGuests`.

findings.title: No check for cancelled or rejected booking status before adding guests
findings.body: The handler fetches the booking and proceeds to add guests without verifying `booking.status`. Adding guests to a cancelled or rejected booking is logically incorrect and could cause confusion (emails sent about a booking that no longer exists, calendar events updated for a cancelled meeting, etc.). A guard such as `if (booking.status === 'CANCELLED' || booking.status === 'REJECTED') throw ...` is missing.

findings.title: isInvalidEmail state not reset on successful submission
findings.body: When `handleAdd` succeeds (validation passes and mutation fires), `setIsInvalidEmail(false)` is never called. If a user first triggers a validation error, then corrects the input and successfully submits, the red error banner will persist in the UI the next time the dialog is opened (assuming the component is not unmounted). The `onSuccess` callback resets `multiEmailValue` but not `isInvalidEmail`.

findings.title: Race condition between attendee existence check and insert
findings.body: The handler reads existing attendees on line 26, filters out duplicates on line 74, then inserts new attendees on line 92. Between the read and the write, a concurrent request could insert the same guest emails, resulting in duplicate attendee rows. Without a database-level unique constraint on (bookingId, email) or a transaction with row-level locking, this can silently create duplicate attendees.

findings.title: Unsafe access to attendees[0] without null check
findings.body: `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` will throw a TypeError if the attendees array is empty. While a booking should normally have at least one attendee, defensive coding (e.g., optional chaining or a fallback) would prevent a crash in edge cases such as data corruption or a booking with all attendees removed.
